title: Best Weight Loss Apps 2026: Calorie Counters, Coaches & Photos
headline: The best weight loss apps in 2026, compared
h1: The best weight loss apps in 2026, compared
dek: An app can help with four things when you're losing weight: showing what you eat, setting a realistic pace, showing change the scale misses, and keeping you going in week three. We compared Fimbl, Noom, MyFitnessPal, Lose It!, MacroFactor, Cronometer and YAZIO on all four.
description: Fimbl, Noom, MyFitnessPal, Lose It!, MacroFactor, Cronometer and YAZIO compared for weight loss: calorie counting, AI coaches, progress photos and cost.

faq.q: What is the best app for weight loss?
faq.a: It depends on how you like to work. On iPhone, we recommend Fimbl for most people: an AI calorie counter with a realistic plan, a weight trend, private progress photos and a coach that reads your own days. Noom is the strongest structured programme, MacroFactor has the best adaptive calorie targets, and MyFitnessPal has the largest food database.

faq.q: What is the best free weight loss app?
faq.a: Fimbl's free version has no ads and includes the food diary, barcode scanner, a calorie plan, macro goals, weight trend, check-ins and progress photos, plus 3 AI photo scans. It's iPhone and iPad only. On Android, Cronometer and YAZIO have free barcode scanners, and MyFitnessPal and Lose It! offer free calorie budgets, all with ads.

faq.q: Do calorie counting apps work for weight loss?
faq.a: They can help. Reviews of weight loss research consistently link self-monitoring what you eat with losing more weight, and logging more often goes with better results, though most of this evidence is observational. Being consistent matters more than being exact, so choose an app that's quick enough to keep using.

faq.q: Which weight loss app has progress photos?
faq.a: Fimbl has free guided progress photos stored only on your iPhone, with side-by-side and swipe compare, a time-lapse and your weight alongside. MyFitnessPal lets you add one photo per weigh-in, MacroFactor includes front, side and back photos in its subscription, and Cronometer has Snapshots. See our full progress photo app comparison.

faq.q: How much weight is it safe to lose in a month?
faq.a: The NHS suggests aiming for 0.5 to 1 kg (1 to 2 lb) a week, which works out at roughly 2 to 4 kg a month. Progress usually slows as your body adapts. If you're pregnant, under 18, have a medical condition, take medication that affects your weight or have a history of disordered eating, talk to a doctor first.

faq.q: Is Fimbl good for weight loss?
faq.a: Yes, if you're on iPhone or iPad and want to steer it yourself. Six short questions set a daily calorie goal at a gentle pace of about 0.5 kg a week or a faster one of about 1 kg a week, and Fimbl turns the faster plan off if it would go below what your body needs at rest. It adds photo calorie scans, macro goals, a weight trend, progress photos and a coach. It isn't a medical programme and doesn't offer human coaches.

faq.q: Why has my weight stopped dropping?
faq.a: Weight naturally moves through the week, and water, food and new muscle can all hide fat loss for a while. Your body also uses less energy as you get lighter, so progress slows over time. Look at the trend over several weeks along with progress photos and how your clothes fit before changing your plan.
